state_background_check.value: Missouri does have an active state felony-disqualification law for candidates, RSMo §115.306.1: no person who has been found guilty of or pled guilty to a felony (federal, Missouri, or an out-of-state offense that would be a felony in Missouri) may qualify as a candidate for 'elective public office' in Missouri. RSMo §115.013 defines 'public office' broadly enough to textually reach federal officeholders ('any employment under the United States, the state of Missouri, or any political subdivision or special district thereof'), and Missouri courts do actively enforce §115.306 — e.g., Fletcher v. Young, 689 S.W.3d 161 (Mo. banc 2024), held a felony guilty plea disqualifies a candidate even after a gubernatorial pardon. However, as applied to a candidate for the U.S. House or Senate specifically, this state law almost certainly cannot be constitutionally enforced. Under U.S. Term Limits, Inc. v. Thornton, 514 U.S. 779 (1995), the Constitution's Qualifications Clauses (Art. I, §2, cl. 2 for the House; Art. I, §3, cl. 3 for the Senate — age, citizenship, inhabitancy) are the exclusive qualifications for congressional service, and a state cannot add to them, directly or indirectly (including through ballot-access denial). No Missouri-specific court decision was found applying §115.306 to a federal congressional candidate (Fletcher v. Young concerns a non-federal office), so this conclusion rests on the general federal constitutional doctrine of Thornton rather than a Missouri-specific ruling — flagged for legal review if certainty is required.
state_background_check.snippet: 115.306. Disqualification as candidate for elective public office, when — filing of affidavit, contents — tax delinquency, effect of. — 1. No person shall qualify as a candidate for elective public office in the state of Missouri who has been found guilty of or pled guilty to a felony under the federal laws of the United States of America or to a felony under the laws of this state or an offense committed in another state that would be considered a felony in this state.

bio_summary.value: I am a father, retired Army officer, and an IT security professional. I have lived in Missouri since I was twelve. I have a degree in history from Missouri State University and I minored in economics. I am not a politician. If elected my children will stay in Missouri and I will make every effort to be home whenever possible.

high_school.snippet: Josh Smead graduated from Harrisonburg High School.

college.value: Bachelor's degree, James Madison University (2012); graduate degree, Iowa State University (2016)
college.snippet: He earned a bachelor's degree from James Madison University in 2012 and a graduate degree from Iowa State University in 2016.

platform.value: Says Missouri farmers are squeezed by rising costs and falling prices across commodities, made worse by shifting trade policy and stalled export programs
platform.snippet: Missouri farmers feed the world, but too many are being squeezed by rising costs and falling prices — not just for grain, but across the board.  From soybeans to hogs to dairy, it’s getting harder to break even, especially with trade policy flipping back and forth and key export programs stalled.

platform.value: Says new agricultural technology only helps if farmers have the right to repair their own equipment and the infrastructure to compete
platform.snippet: New technology can help, but only if farmers have the right to repair their own equipment and the infrastructure to compete.

platform.value: Favors what he calls smart trade over bailouts, and policies that put small and family-run farms first
platform.snippet: I believe in smart trade, not bailouts — and policies that put small and family-run farms first.

platform.value: Says North Missouri needs energy that is reliable, affordable and built for the long haul
platform.snippet: North Missouri needs energy that’s reliable, affordable, and built for the long haul.

platform.value: Supports the Grain Belt Express transmission project as delivering stable, low-cost power to Missouri communities while strengthening the grid against blackouts and extreme weather
platform.snippet: Projects like the Grain Belt Express offer exactly that — stable, low-cost power delivered to dozens of Missouri communities while strengthening our grid against blackouts and extreme weather.

platform.value: Would invest in infrastructure that keeps costs down rather than blocking projects for short-term politics
platform.snippet: We should be investing in infrastructure that keeps the lights on and the bills low, not blocking progress for short-term politics.

platform.value: Says the Postal Service is a service rather than a profit machine and should not be gutted for failing to turn one
platform.snippet: The U.S. Postal Service is a service — not a profit machine.  Just like we do not ask if the military turns a profit, we should not gut the Postal Service for failing to make one.

platform.value: Opposes privatizing the Postal Service, saying it would slash rural delivery, and that affordable, reliable mail should be protected rather than sold off
platform.snippet: For decades, there has been a push to privatize it, which would slash rural delivery and abandon millions of Americans.  The Postal Service is part of our national identity — affordable, reliable mail should be protected, not sold off.

platform.value: Would strengthen Medicaid rather than cut it, noting one in five Missourians rely on it
platform.snippet: We need to strengthen Medicaid, not slash it, and invest in rural healthcare so families can grow and age in the communities they love.

platform.value: Says families in parts of the 6th District drive over an hour to reach a delivery room and some rural hospitals are near closing, and that healthcare access shouldn't depend on ZIP code
platform.snippet: In parts of the 6th District, families already drive over an hour just to reach a delivery room — and some rural hospitals are on the brink of closing for good.

platform.value: Says healthcare access should not depend on where someone lives
platform.snippet: Healthcare access shouldn’t depend on your ZIP code.

platform.value: Says Missourians deserve sovereignty over their own bodies and that he trusts them to make personal decisions rather than the government
platform.snippet: Missourians deserve sovereignty over their own bodies — plain and simple.

platform.value: Says he trusts Missourians to make personal decisions for themselves rather than the government
platform.snippet: I trust Missourians to make personal decisions for themselves — not the government.

platform.value: Says climate change is real and Missouri is already feeling it through hotter summers, more extreme winters and stronger winds
platform.snippet: Climate change is real, and Missouri is already feeling it — hotter summers, more extreme winters, and stronger winds.

platform.value: Argues the conditions on the ground call for a smarter approach regardless of whether one believes in climate change, and that resilient communities require long-term thinking over short-term fixes
platform.snippet: Whether you believe in climate change or not, the reality on the ground calls for a smarter approach.  As a builder, I know it’s cheaper in the long run to build things right the first time.  The same goes for environmental policy: resilient communities start with long-term thinking, not short-term fixes.

platform.value: Says tariffs have become a political tool whose cost falls on working families rather than foreign governments, catching American farmers and consumers in the trade war
platform.snippet: Tariffs have become a political tool, but too often it’s working families — not foreign governments — who pay the price. Today’s shoot-from-the-hip arbitrary tariffs and the growing trade war means American farmers and consumers keep getting caught in the crossfire.

platform.value: Says Congress should stop protecting the powerful and invest in people, citing record household debt alongside tax breaks and subsidies for billionaires
platform.snippet: Meanwhile, household debt just hit a record $17.3 trillion, and billionaires still enjoy tax breaks and subsidies. It’s time Congress stopped protecting the powerful and started investing in the people.

platform.value: Would protect family farms and expand access to markets, saying farmers are squeezed by monopolies and rising costs
platform.snippet: Northern Missouri’s economy starts with agriculture, but our farmers are being squeezed by monopolies and rising costs. I’ll fight to protect family farms, expand access to markets, and support sustainable practices like soil health, water conservation, and ag-tech innovation.

platform.value: Frames investment in long-term stewardship of the land as how the future of farming is secured for the next generation
platform.snippet: Investing in long-term stewardship of the land isn’t just good policy—it’s how we secure the future of farming for the next generation.

platform.value: Would expand access to affordable healthcare, capital and federal contracts for local businesses
platform.snippet: I’ll fight to expand access to affordable healthcare, capital, and federal contracts for local businesses.

platform.value: Says small businesses are left behind while billion-dollar corporations receive tax breaks and bailouts, and calls for leveling the playing field
platform.snippet: Small businesses are the backbone of Northern Missouri’s economy, but too often they’re left behind while billion-dollar corporations get tax breaks and bailouts.

platform.value: Would fight for federal funding that reaches rural towns rather than only urban centers, covering roads, bridges, water systems and flood control
platform.snippet: Rural infrastructure has been neglected for too long—roads, bridges, water systems, and flood control need urgent investment.  I’ll fight for federal funding that reaches rural towns, not just urban centers, and supports the basics that families and small businesses rely on.

platform.value: Would fully fund rural broadband expansion across fiber, cable, satellite and wireless so every home and town is connected
platform.snippet: We need to fully fund rural broadband expansion and explore all options—from traditional fiber and cable to satellite and wireless solutions—so every home and town gets connected.

platform.value: Says broadband investment must prioritize unserved areas rather than padding profits for major telecoms
platform.snippet: This investment must prioritize unserved areas, not just pad profits for major telecoms.

platform.value: Says everyone deserves to live freely and equally, and that who someone loves or how they identify is not the government's business
platform.snippet: Everyone deserves to live freely and equally — no exceptions. I believe in a government that protects rights, not one that polices personal lives. Who someone loves or how they identify is none of the government’s business, and it certainly shouldn’t be a political weapon.

platform.value: Would stand for equal protection under the law and against attempts to use power to divide, discriminate or interfere in private lives
platform.snippet: I will always stand for equal protection under the law, and against any attempt to use power to divide, discriminate, or interfere in people’s private lives.

platform.value: Supports the Second Amendment, saying it works to keep tyrants at bay, and that public safety can be protected without trampling those freedoms
platform.snippet: I support and appreciate the Second Amendment because it works to keep tyrants at bay.

platform.value: Would require background checks on gun sales, encourage safe storage, and document gun transactions
platform.snippet: That means requiring background checks on gun sales, encouraging safe storage, and documenting gun transactions.

platform.value: Argues that since car and house sales are documented, keeping a basic record when a deadly weapon changes hands makes sense
platform.snippet: We document car sales and house sales – it just makes sense to keep a basic record when a deadly weapon changes hands. Responsible gun ownership is part of our culture — and common sense reforms help keep it that way.

platform.value: Believes the draft should include all able-bodied men and women
platform.snippet: I believe the Draft should include all able bodied Men & Women.

platform.value: Describes himself as proudly pro-union, saying workers deserve a real voice, fair wages and the freedom to organize without interference
platform.snippet: I’m proudly pro-union because workers deserve a real voice, fair wages, and the freedom to organize without interference.

platform.value: Says federal actions are chipping away at labor rights, gutting contracts and making it harder for workers including federal employees to unionize
platform.snippet: Today, federal actions are chipping away at labor rights, gutting contracts, and making it harder for workers — including federal employees — to unionize.

platform.value: Says unstable tariff policy drives up material costs mid-project for trades and small contractors, and that rebuilding American industry means strengthening unions rather than undercutting them
platform.snippet: At the same time, unstable tariff policy is hitting trades and small contractors hard, driving up material costs in the middle of projects and threatening their ability to stay profitable. If we’re serious about rebuilding American industry and protecting working families, we need to strengthen unions — not undercut them.

platform.value: Supports term limits for politicians, saying he is an architect who does not plan to be a politician for the rest of his career
platform.snippet: I support term limits for politicians. I am an architect, and being a politician is not what I plan to do for the rest of my career. Career politicians who spend decades in office become detached from the reality the rest of us face every day.

bio_summary.value: I have lived in Missouri since 2017, and most importantly, this is where my four young children call home. My wife and I are building our lives and our small business here – literally constructing our first building in Liberty as part of our growing company. Missouri isn’t just where I live; it’s where I’m invested in the future, for my family, and for everyone in the 6th District.

employment_record.value: Radio Host KXCV/KRNW, New Reporter KCMO, Talk Radio Host Congressman Sam Graves, Field Representative/Deputy Communications Director
employment_record.snippet: Radio Host KXCV/KRNW, New Reporter KCMO, Talk Radio Host Congressman Sam Graves, Field Representative/Deputy Communications Director

platform.value: Supports protecting constitutional rights of law-abiding gun owners and will oppose efforts to restrict those rights through federal overreach, defending the right to keep and bear arms while ensuring criminals are held accountable for violent crime
platform.snippet: I support President Trump's commitment to protecting the constitutional rights of law-abiding gun owners and will oppose efforts to restrict those rights through federal overreach. In Congress, I will fight to defend our right to keep and bear arms while ensuring criminals, not responsible citizens, are held accountable for violent crime.

platform.value: Will work to reduce red tape, expand access to care, strengthen rural hospitals, and ensure families in small towns can access quality healthcare close to home
platform.snippet: I will work alongside President Trump to reduce red tape, expand access to care, strengthen rural hospitals, and ensure families in small towns can access quality healthcare close to home.

platform.value: Proudly pro-life, supports policies that defend the unborn, support mothers and families, will oppose taxpayer funding for abortion and support efforts that protect innocent life
platform.snippet: I am proudly pro-life and believe every human life is a gift from God that deserves protection. I support policies that defend the unborn, support mothers and families, and promote a culture that values life at every stage. While abortion policy is increasingly being decided at the state level, I will oppose taxpayer funding for abortion and support efforts that protect innocent life.

platform.value: Supports making President Trump's tax cuts permanent and will fight against any effort to raise taxes on hardworking Americans
platform.snippet: I support making President Trump's tax cuts permanent and will fight against any effort to raise taxes on hardworking Americans.

platform.value: Supports efforts to expand market access, strengthen domestic food production, and reduce burdensome regulations that hurt family farms, will fight for a seat on the House Agriculture Committee
platform.snippet: I support President Trump's efforts to expand market access, strengthen domestic food production, and reduce burdensome regulations that hurt family farms. I will fight for a seat on the House Agriculture Committee to ensure Missouri agriculture remains competitive and prosperous for future generations.

platform.value: Supports efforts to make America the world leader in cryptocurrency and digital asset innovation, will fight to protect financial freedom, encourage responsible innovation, and oppose burdensome regulations
platform.snippet: I support President Trump's efforts to make America the world leader in cryptocurrency and digital asset innovation. Washington bureaucrats should not stifle innovation with burdensome regulations that drive jobs and investment overseas. I will fight to protect financial freedom, encourage responsible innovation, and ensure America, not China, leads the future of digital finance.

platform.value: Supports efforts to secure the border, finish the wall, end catch-and-release policies, and deport dangerous criminal illegal immigrants
platform.snippet: I support President Trump's efforts to secure the border, finish the wall, end catch-and-release policies, and deport dangerous criminal illegal immigrants.

platform.value: Supports the SAVE Act to ensure only American citizens can vote in federal elections
platform.snippet: I also support the SAVE Act to ensure only American citizens can vote in federal elections.

bio_summary.value: Chris Stigall was born in Richmond, Missouri . Stigall earned a bachelor's degree from Northwest Missouri State University. His career experience includes working in conservative talk radio and serving as a field representative and deputy communications director for Congressman Sam Graves. [1]
